change.title: 4 changes: Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com) and more

source.quote: The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]

tasks.reasoning:
This one task covers all 4 coinbase-pro changes that affect this repo. Handle every one of them in this single change set, prove each with your test, and say in finish which you changed and which needed no change.

1. Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com) (product-shutdown, effective 2024-09-11)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md
   Quote: The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]
   Affects: operations: api.pro.coinbase.com
   Call sites: strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js:17 (websocketURI points to ws-feed.pro.coinbase.com / ws-feed-public.sandbox.pro.coinbase.com; must move to ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com (and the exchange sandbox feed).); strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js:46 (AuthenticatedClient built with apiURI api.pro.coinbase.com / api-public.sandbox.pro.coinbase.com; must point at api.exchange.coinbase.com / api-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com.); strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js:81 (WebsocketClient ticker feed connects to the deprecated Pro websocket host.); strategies/momentumTradingWithStopLoss/momentumTradingWithStopLoss.js:82 (WebsocketClient ticker feed and AuthenticatedClient in this strategy use the deprecated Pro hosts.); strategies/reverseMomentumTrading/reverseMomentumTrading.js:81 (WebsocketClient ticker feed and AuthenticatedClient in this strategy use the deprecated Pro hosts.); coinbaseProLibrary.js:106 (GET /profiles is sent to apiURI on api.pro.coinbase.com.); coinbaseProLibrary.js:152 (GET /fees is sent to apiURI on api.pro.coinbase.com.); coinbaseProLibrary.js:210 (POST /profiles/transfer is sent to apiURI on api.pro.coinbase.com.); buyAndSell.js:57 (placeOrder/getOrder/cancelOrder calls via the coinbase-pro SDK AuthenticatedClient go to the deprecated Pro REST host.)
   Why it applies: Every API path in the repo targets the deprecated Pro hosts. That covers the coinbase-pro 0.9.0 SDK (REST AuthenticatedClient and WebsocketClient ticker feeds in all three strategies) and the axios-based coinbaseProLibrary.js (profiles, fees, profile transfer). The SDK's default and the configured apiURI/websocketURI values are api.pro.coinbase.com, ws-feed.pro.coinbase.com and their sandbox equivalents. The deprecation took effect 2024-09-11, so the bot cannot trade, read accounts or stream prices until these hosts are switched to api.exchange.coinbase.com, ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com and the exchange sandbox hosts. The migration agent should update every apiURI/websocketURI constant (real and sandbox via TRADING_ENV) across all strategies and coinbaseProLibrary.js. It should also check whether the unmaintained coinbase-pro npm SDK still works against the Exchange host when passed the new URIs; the Exchange API is wire-compatible, with the same CB-ACCESS HMAC signing. Replacing the SDK is a fallback if it does not.

2. Coinbase Exchange domain only accepts TLS 1.2 or higher (other, effective 2025-10-20)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md
   Quote: This means that any client applications, trading bots, or other automated systems that currently rely on older versions of TLS (such as TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1) will no longer be able to establish a secure connection with the Coinbase Exchange domain.
   Call sites: coinbaseProLibrary.js:106 (axios HTTPS requests to the Exchange domain must negotiate TLS 1.2+.); strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js:46 (coinbase-pro SDK REST and websocket connections must negotiate TLS 1.2+.)
   Why it applies: The bot connects to the Coinbase Exchange domain over HTTPS (axios 0.21.4 and the coinbase-pro SDK's request/ws stack) and over WSS. Node.js 12+ defaults to TLS 1.2 or higher, so this is likely already fine. The repo's Node runtime is not pinned here, though, and an old Node (<12) or a custom secureProtocol/minVersion override would fail after 2025-10-20. The migration agent should check the engines field, the Dockerfile or CI Node version, and any TLS agent options, and pin Node >=12 (preferably a current LTS) if needed.

3. Transfer funds between profiles now returns transfer_id instead of an empty 200 body (other, effective 2026-10-13)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md
   Quote: The [Transfer funds between profiles)](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/exchange-api/rest-api/profiles/transfer-funds-profile.md) REST endpoint now returns the `transfer_id` in a 200 successful response. Previously, we returned an empty 200 response.
   Affects: fields: transfer_id
   Call sites: coinbaseProLibrary.js:210 (POST /profiles/transfer returns result.data, which changes from an empty body to an object containing transfer_id.); buyAndSell.js:102 (Caller of the profile transfer; any logic that assumes an empty response or tests the response for emptiness would change behaviour.)
   Why it applies: The repo calls the Transfer funds between profiles endpoint and returns result.data to buyAndSell.js. The response is additive (transfer_id instead of an empty 200), so most code keeps working. The migration agent should verify that neither the caller nor the library treats a non-empty response as unexpected or tries to parse the body strictly. It may optionally log or store transfer_id.

4. Opt-in portfolio isolation for API keys: keys without cross portfolio access get limited results/403/404 (release TBD) (auth-change)
   Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md
   Quote: When on, keys without **cross portfolio access** are limited to their own portfolio.
   Affects: operations: GET /profiles, GET /accounts/all
   Call sites: coinbaseProLibrary.js:106 (GET /profiles would return only the key's own portfolio for keys without cross portfolio access, breaking the strategies' profile lookup.); coinbaseProLibrary.js:210 (POST /profiles/transfer moves funds between profiles and would get 403/404 without cross portfolio access.); strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js:241 (getAccounts results could be limited to the key's portfolio.)
   Why it applies: The bot depends on cross-profile behaviour: it lists profiles (GET /profiles), looks up accounts, and transfers profits between profiles via POST /profiles/transfer. Once portfolio isolation is switched on (opt-in, release date TBD), an API key without cross portfolio access would see only its own portfolio and get 403/404 on cross-profile operations, so the profit-transfer flow breaks. The migration agent should document that the API key needs cross portfolio access. It should also add clear error handling for 403/404 on profile lookups and transfers. There is no firm date; impact depends on account settings.

record.prBody:
## 4 changes: Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com) and more [Verified]

### Change

Swapped the Pro hosts for Exchange hosts (REST and websocket, real and sandbox) in the three strategy files. The axios helper and the SDK clients take their base URL from those constants, so they needed no other edit. buyAndSell.js now logs the profile transfer result as JSON plus transfer_id. README docs links point to the CDP docs. Not changed: the TLS 1.2 requirement (Node 22 default, no TLS overrides in the code) and portfolio isolation (opt-in, no date). Portfolio isolation does mean the API key will need cross portfolio access once it is switched on. The transfer_id change takes effect 2026-10-13 and is already handled: coinbaseProLibrary.js already returns result.data, so only the log line changed.

Files touched:
- `README.md`
- `buyAndSell.js`
- `strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js`
- `strategies/momentumTradingWithStopLoss/momentumTradingWithStopLoss.js`
- `strategies/reverseMomentumTrading/reverseMomentumTrading.js`
- `test_hosts.js`

### Why

api.pro.coinbase.com and its websocket and sandbox hosts are shut down, so every REST and websocket call in the bot would fail.

> The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]

Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hosts | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- hosts, added by the agent: `node test_hosts.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `hosts`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Live connectivity and HMAC signing on Exchange hosts
- The coinbase-pro SDK 0.9.0 working unchanged against Exchange hosts
- Sandbox host names not confirmed in the docs
- Pro API keys may need reissuing on Exchange
- No 403/404 handling was added for portfolio isolation
- The test is static (reads source files) and does not run the code
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- All REST and websocket traffic now goes to Exchange hosts
- The transfer result debug log now prints JSON and transfer_id

---

review.summary: The diff swaps the hardcoded hosts in the three strategy files to the exchange hosts, which handles the main deprecation. It does not show the coinbaseProLibrary.js edits, and it adds an unrelated logging change in buyAndSell.js. The only check is a string-matching test, which does not exercise any API calls. 'Verified' is too strong. Pre-existing and out of scope: the README still says to comment out sandbox variables, which no longer matches the code.

concerns.issue: The named call sites (GET /profiles, GET /fees, POST /profiles/transfer at lines 106/152/210) are not changed. They take apiURI from the constructor, so they probably inherit the new host. But the file was not shown, and it may have a hardcoded host or default URI, or sign requests against the old host. Please confirm this; the diff alone does not show it.

The deprecated `coinbase-pro` npm client is still used for AuthenticatedClient and WebsocketClient, now pointed at the exchange hosts. Nothing confirms that it works against api.exchange.coinbase.com. The sandbox hostnames (api-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com, ws-feed-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com) and the Exchange auth/signing requirements should be checked against the changelog or docs. The same applies to the other two strategy files. The WebSocket feed may also now require auth or different channel handling.

The change to the transfer logging (reading transferResult.transfer_id and JSON.stringify of the result) is not required by the host migration. Its indentation is off (extra space). The assumption that the response has a `transfer_id` field is unconfirmed. The test only asserts the string appears in source.

The check only greps source files for host strings. It does not touch coinbaseProLibrary.js, buyAndSell.js call paths, REST, WebSocket or auth. It also adds a stray test file at the repo root, outside any test runner. Nothing proves that order, account, product or websocket calls work on the new host, so the 'verified' grade is not supported.

checkFirst: Open coinbaseProLibrary.js and check for any hardcoded or default pro.coinbase.com URIs and how request signing builds the URL.
Run the bot in the sandbox against the new exchange hosts: getAccounts, getProducts, placeOrder/getOrder/cancelOrder, the ticker websocket, and the /profiles, /fees and transfer calls.
Confirm in the quoted changelog or Exchange docs that the sandbox hostnames used are correct and that the coinbase-pro client's auth works unchanged.
Check whether the transfer response really returns `transfer_id` or whether that logging change should be reverted.
Grep the whole repo (analyzers, index.js, other strategies) for remaining pro.coinbase.com references.
